source_identity.title: Polynuclear growth and the Toda lattice

summary: Three Major problems affect a core abstract theorem, normalization of the stated PNG equation, and a principal proof dependency. One Minor problem concerns the narrow-wedge initial velocity. Correctly normalized intended PNG results are not thereby refuted.
limitations: Focused proof and counterexample review, not a certification of every argument on 71 pages.
No complete repaired PNG theorem or replacement generator argument is proved.
Bounded correction search did not identify an erratum; this is not proof of absence or priority.
No author code was run; code absence is not a mathematical defect.
Native helpers contributed bounded checks; no independent human acceptance or verified backend identity is claimed.

K0=P/2,K1=K2=0 are constant finite rank, all required trace-norm derivatives exist.

problems.result: The lowest-interior-index conclusion is false as stated; mixed identity (3.4) is not implied there.
problems.counterevidence: The remaining inspected resolvent algebra is consistent conditional on the missing mixed identity; no failure of a strengthened theorem established.
problems.impact: Section3.2 uses lower=-1 upper=1 targetr=0, precisely the affected endpoint. Central mechanism compromised as stated.

problems.repair_verification: Specific missing-hypothesis mechanism checked; complete repaired PNG theorem not verified.

checks.reason: For lower=0, upper=2 and constant K0=P/2, K1=K2=0, every stipulated shift kills P's (1,1) support and every required trace-norm derivative vanishes. Q=(2,1,1) has all inverses. The Toda residual at r=1 is exactly -1/2, while alleged (3.4) would require 0=P/2. The actual three-layer PNG application is at the same lowest interior index, so merely restricting the theorem removes that application. No refutation of a strengthened theorem or intended PNG model is claimed.

With one spatial point, t=eta+zeta and x=eta-zeta imply the mixed derivative is the full wave operator. Direct Poisson/permutation expansion gives F1=1-s^2/4+s^3/9+O(s^4), F2=1-s^3/36+O(s^4) and residual 3s+O(s^2). r=1 exceeds the deterministic threshold; adjacent determinants remain positive. Root checked the retained rational program's permutation counting, interval operations, positive denominators and factorial tail bound against its genuine exit-0 historical execution; it was not rerun or relabeled a current execution. Correct half-vector-field normalization is counterevidence for the intended theorem, not validity of the printed equation.

The thin closed islands have distinct locally finite unit jumps and h_m(0)=1; the actual hypograph recovery/limsup criteria give h_m -> 1 despite average threshold indicators tending to 1 instead of 0. No uniform jump-count assumption excludes them. The shock datum also gives average exp(-2t0^2)/2 while the point probability is zero. Almost-everywhere convergence under the invariant measure may repair the latter, but cannot establish C0 membership. Equations (4.20), (4.25), Proposition 4.8 and Theorem 2.3 form the actual proof chain. This is a central proof gap, not a Fredholm-formula counterexample.

For r=0, integrating the exact deficit against a smooth compact test function is bounded by (4/3)||phi|| t^3; division by t gives zero, also for all r>=0 by monotonicity. For r<0 the expanding excluded interval yields -2 delta_0. The correct restriction is -2*1_{r<0} delta_0. The multi-unit-jump example remains conditional on the broader reading of 'simple cases'. These displayed initial data are not used by the inspected Fredholm proof.
